meta.description: Normalized membrane-separation materials agent library built on top of the legacy gcmc_agent workspace.
meta.generated_notice: Generated from registry/catalog.json. Do not hand-edit generated md files.

skills.title: Harness Maintenance
skills.use_when: Use when the user wants to audit, extend, synchronize, or rebuild the BiMemAgent harness itself.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to run adsorption, cDFT, diffusion, or DFT workloads directly.
skills.automation: Route into the harness-maintainer agent and update registry/catalog.json plus generated assets.
notes: This imports the legacy meta-skill for harness design and maintenance.
Use it for agent or skill synchronization work rather than scientific compute requests.
Treat the harness as a living system: fold repeated debugging fixes, stable workflows, and reusable plotting/reporting patterns back into skills, docs, and config.

skills.title: System Overview
skills.use_when: Use at the start of a membrane-material task to choose the right method, backend, and follow-up skill.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to run calculations directly.
skills.automation: Route into the lead orchestrator and select a method-specific skill.
notes: This is the default trigger skill for broad design or screening requests.
If a domain skill already exists for the task, route into that skill before probing raw executables, PATH entries, or backend binaries from the shell.

skills.title: CIF Registry
skills.use_when: Use when the agent needs to locate, disambiguate, or validate CIF files.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to infer physical properties or run simulations.
notes: Backed by helper.find_cif().

skills.title: Paper Retrieval
skills.use_when: Use when the user provides a DOI, arXiv id, or PDF URL and wants the paper pulled into the workflow.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for scientific interpretation without reading the retrieved paper or RAG context.
notes: Backed by helper.fetch_paper().

skills.title: Literature RAG
skills.use_when: Use when the user asks for mechanism explanation, literature comparison, parameter recommendations, expected performance, or gas-specific evidence across any membrane-separation gas system and the answer should be grounded in the local paper vector index.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to download papers, run simulations, or replace quantitative analysis of completed result files.
notes: Backed by the legacy rag/ vector index through helper.search_kb semantics.
This skill runs the query through the dedicated Agent conda environment so retrieval does not depend on the current shell Python.
It supports query routing for overview, methods, mechanism, benchmark, parameter, and material-lookup questions.
It is gas-agnostic and should be used for CO2, CH4, N2, H2, Xe/Kr, H2S/SO2, light hydrocarbons, and other membrane-separation gas systems covered by the corpus.
Trigger it before answering mechanism, benchmark, or simulation-parameter questions that need literature support.

skills.title: Adsorption Workflow
skills.use_when: Use for GCMC isotherms, batch comparisons, or Henry-constant calculations.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for PBS job-state monitoring or result interpretation.
notes: Backed by helper.run_isotherm(), helper.run_batch(), helper.run_henry().
When the user is asking about adsorption or GCMC behavior, prefer this skill surface over shell-level probing of RASPA binaries.

skills.title: Cluster Jobs
skills.use_when: Use to submit or inspect PBS-based adsorption jobs.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to interpret completed scientific results.
notes: Backed by helper.submit_job() and helper.check_job().
The legacy single-job submit path is currently brittle and should be repaired upstream.

skills.title: Result Files
skills.use_when: Use after a run to navigate output folders, plots, CSV files, and logs.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to launch new runs.
notes: Supports structured inspection of filesystem result paths, PBS job artifacts, and BiMemAgent ledger runs.

skills.title: Nature Figure Workflow
skills.use_when: Use when the user wants publication-grade plots, multi-panel figures, figure-ready data curation, or journal-ready SVG/PDF/TIFF exports from BiMemAgent results.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for launching simulations or for dashboard-style interactive plotting.
skills.automation: Route into the scientific-communicator or figure-specific workflow after results are available.
notes: Backed by the global nature-figure skill.
Use after `results` or `analysis` when the project needs publication-quality visual output rather than raw CSV inspection.
This is the preferred path for data-to-figure cleanup, panel design, and manuscript-ready exports.

skills.title: Full Paper Reader
skills.use_when: Use when the user wants a paper translated, read closely, or converted into a source-grounded bilingual Markdown artifact with figure/table placement.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use when a short summary or citation list is sufficient.
inputs: pdf, doi, arxiv id, or pasted text
skills.automation: Route into the scientific-communicator when full-paper reading or bilingual extraction is requested.
notes: Backed by the global nature-reader skill.
Use this instead of ad hoc summarization when the user explicitly wants source-grounded full-paper reading.

skills.title: Nature Citation Support
skills.use_when: Use when the user wants Nature/CNS-style supporting references, claim-to-reference mapping, or reference-manager-ready citation exports.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use as a substitute for the local membrane-separation RAG when the request is about internal corpus retrieval only.
skills.automation: Route into the scientific-communicator for citation mining and export.
notes: Backed by the global nature-citation skill.
Use this for manuscript support and claim-level citation work; use `literature-rag` for the local membrane-separation paper database.

skills.title: Nature Writing
skills.use_when: Use when the user wants abstracts, results narratives, discussions, or manuscript sections written or restructured from BiMemAgent outputs.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for raw calculation submission or low-level file inspection.
skills.automation: Route into the scientific-communicator after scientific analysis is complete.
notes: Backed by the global nature-writing skill.
Use after `analysis`, `results`, and `nature-figure` when the user wants paper-ready prose.

skills.title: Scientific Analysis
skills.use_when: Use after calculations finish and the agent needs quantitative interpretation or ranking.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to negotiate run parameters or monitor cluster state.
notes: Backed by helper.analyze().

skills.title: Charge Assignment
skills.use_when: Use before polar-gas GCMC or cDFT runs that require charged CIFs.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use as a substitute for cDFT or GCMC execution.
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: The wrapper emits a deterministic PACMAN execution plan.
When run with --execute, BiMemAgent also copies generated *_pacman.cif files into the declared output_dir.

skills.title: cDFT Workflow
skills.use_when: Use for classical DFT adsorption workflows, especially batch screening and average-density calculations.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to explain finished results without analysis context.
inputs: bulk_densities or total pressure plus mole fractions
notes: Backed by helper.run_cdft_pipeline().
Legacy code still needs isolated input directories for safe parallel execution.

skills.title: Pore Analysis
skills.use_when: Use when PLD, LCD, void fraction, pore volume, or surface area are required.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to rank materials unless the analysis agent asks for the descriptors.
notes: Backed by tools.zeopp.run_single() and run_batch().

skills.title: Material Properties
skills.use_when: Use when element composition or derived chemistry features are needed for screening or ML.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to infer adsorption behavior by itself.
notes: Backed by tools.mof_features.extract_features() and extract_features_batch().

skills.title: Interaction Energy
skills.use_when: Use when the workflow needs a binding-energy estimate or mechanism probe.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use as a full DFT workflow.
notes: Backed by analysis.interaction.calc_binding_energy().

skills.title: MD Optimization
skills.use_when: Use for LAMMPS-based geometry relaxation or MD annealing.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use when only a fast adsorption estimate is needed.
notes: Backed by tools.lammps_optimize.run_single(), run_md(), and run_batch().

skills.title: xTB Optimization
skills.use_when: Use for molecular or cluster-level xTB geometry optimization and lightweight electronic-structure cleanup.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for periodic framework MD or as a substitute for VASP on extended solids.
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: Backed by scripts/run_xtb_optimize.py and the configured xTB executable.
Current wrapper targets molecule/cluster jobs; periodic framework cleanup should still use md-optimize.

skills.title: Guest Forcefield
skills.use_when: Use when a single guest molecule must be parameterized into reusable RASPA force-field assets or when a mixed-guest RASPA case bundle must be written around those assets.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for framework charge assignment, framework property extraction, or full adsorption execution.
inputs: guest molecule path or framework case inputs
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: Canonical name is guest-forcefield; molecule-forcefield-pipeline remains a compatibility alias for the incubated skill name.
Build action packages one guest molecule into RASPA guest definitions backed by LigParGen outputs.
Case action writes mix.input, PBS submission text, and an optional PACMAN-to-RASPA wrapper without replacing the existing charge or adsorption skills.

Framework charges come from PACMOF/PACMAN or an approved charged CIF, independently of UFF/OPLS. Normalize-cif is read-only validation requiring declared expected_net_charge and charge_source; it never rewrites charges or forces neutrality.

skills.title: String TST Diffusion
skills.use_when: Use for diffusion coefficients, migration barriers, or transition-path calculations.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for adsorption equilibria.
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: The wrapper emits a deterministic String-method plan using the legacy Slurm scripts.
When run with --execute, BiMemAgent generates input manifests and renders a ready-to-submit Slurm batch script.

skills.title: Structure Generation
skills.use_when: Use to build MOF, COF, or HOF candidates from PORMAKE assets.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use to optimize structures after generation; hand off to md-optimize if needed.
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: The wrapper emits a reproducible command plan against tools/pormake_generate.py.

skills.title: External Potential
skills.use_when: Use for TuTraSt-style external-potential calculations and precomputed Vext fields.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use as a synonym for the main cDFT adsorption pipeline.
skills.automation: python scripts/run_workflow.py --spec <spec.json>  # add --execute to run the generated command
notes: Canonical name is external-potential; tustrast remains a legacy alias.
When run with --execute, BiMemAgent generates Vext inputs, renders a PBS batch script, and wires in local run/collect helpers for the external-potential executable.

skills.title: VASP DFT
skills.use_when: Use for DFT setup, submission, or result parsing with VASP.
skills.do_not_use_for: Do not use for quick force-field-level exploration.
notes: Canonical name is vasp-dft; vasp remains a legacy alias.
Backed by tools.vasp setup/submit/run/parse entrypoints.

agents.title: Lead Orchestrator
agents.role: Own user interaction, method selection, parameter confirmation, task decomposition, and handoff to specialists.
agents.use_when: Use for all broad or ambiguous user requests.
workflow: If the request is a real numerical calculation, prefer scheduler submission over local execution.
If the user asks for mechanisms, benchmarks, or parameter advice, query `literature-rag` first.
If the user asks for paper reading, publication figures, citation support, or manuscript text, route into the Nature-style communication skills instead of improvising.
If this project already has a matching domain skill, use that skill path before probing raw executables or backend binaries from the shell.
Use `xtb-optimize` for linker, adsorbate, or finite-cluster semiempirical cleanup instead of periodic framework MD.
Use `guest-forcefield` when the missing piece is a guest molecule package or mixed-guest RASPA case scaffold rather than framework simulation itself.
Dispatch specialist work or run structured scripts.
Record or reference run ids when workflows are executed.
notes: This is the entry agent for the new harness.
Prefer `scripts/run_workflow.py` over ad hoc shell commands so runs are captured in the ledger.
Trigger `literature-rag` before answering literature-grounded questions instead of relying on memory.
For cluster-type compute, default to submission rather than node01 local execution unless the task is explicitly lightweight and non-computational.
Shell-level probing is a fallback for debugging missing capability, not the default path when a project skill already exists.

agents.title: Harness Maintainer
agents.role: Maintain the BiMemAgent project library itself: skill import coverage, naming normalization, generated markdown drift, and automation-surface consistency.
agents.use_when: Use for harness audits, agent or skill synchronization, naming cleanup, or regeneration work.
workflow: Fold repeated debugging patterns, plotting conventions, and stable workflows back into reusable skills or config.
When the main agent bypasses an existing domain skill and drops to raw shell probing, encode the missing routing rule back into the harness.
Run harness verification before reporting completion.
notes: This is the meta-maintenance agent for the rebuilt project library.
Treat each session as potential training data for the local harness: if a workaround becomes stable, encode it.

agents.title: Project Governor
agents.role: Track project state, maintain run plans, classify failures, and recommend retries or escalations using the BiMemAgent run ledger.
agents.use_when: Use when a multi-step project is underway and run-state management matters.
workflow: Inspect recent runs through the ledger.
Check for blocked or failed tasks.
notes: Separates project governance from raw job monitoring.
Use scripts/project_status.py or runs/index.json as the primary state source.

agents.title: Scientific Communicator
agents.role: Turn BiMemAgent results, literature context, and user notes into publication-grade figures, bilingual paper readers, citation exports, and manuscript-ready text.
agents.use_when: Use when the user asks for paper translation, manuscript support, figure making, data-to-plot cleanup, or citation-grounded writing.
workflow: Clarify whether the task is figure, reader, citation, or writing oriented.
Load the relevant result files or paper sources.
Use `literature-rag` when domain evidence from the local membrane-separation corpus is needed.
Use the Nature-style skills for the final communication artifact.
Return the artifact path plus any remaining scientific gaps.
notes: This agent is for scientific communication rather than raw compute.
Use it after the calculation side of the workflow has produced stable inputs.

agents.title: Adsorption Executor
agents.role: Execute direct adsorption workflows through the normalized runner or legacy helper functions.
agents.use_when: Use after parameters are fixed for GCMC or Henry calculations.
workflow: Run the workflow or emit a dry-run plan.

agents.title: cDFT Executor
agents.role: Execute the main cDFT adsorption pipeline after parameters are negotiated.
agents.use_when: Use for cDFT screening or follow-up validation runs.
workflow: Check whether CIFs are already charged.
Run or dry-run the cDFT wrapper.
notes: Legacy alias vext-executor is preserved for migration.

agents.title: Charge Executor
agents.role: Prepare charged CIFs via PACMAN or emit the exact command plan for charge assignment.
agents.use_when: Use before polar-gas adsorption or cDFT work.
workflow: Emit or execute the PACMAN plan.

agents.title: Pore Executor
agents.role: Compute pore descriptors from Zeo++ for one or many structures.
agents.use_when: Use when structural descriptors are missing.
workflow: Run Zeo++ single or batch mode.

agents.title: Diffusion Executor
agents.role: Prepare or launch String-method diffusion workflows.
agents.use_when: Use for diffusion and migration-barrier tasks.
workflow: Return output locations and scheduler assumptions.
notes: Current automation prepares runnable scheduler assets through command-wrapper execution.

agents.title: MD Optimizer
agents.role: Run LAMMPS-based geometry relaxation or MD cleanup before higher-cost calculations.
agents.use_when: Use when structures require force-field-level cleanup.

agents.title: xTB Executor
agents.role: Prepare or execute molecule-scale xTB optimization jobs through the normalized xTB skill.
agents.use_when: Use when the project needs a fast semiempirical optimization for linkers, adsorbates, or finite clusters.
outputs: command plan or xTB output paths
workflow: Emit or execute the xTB optimization command.
notes: This is intentionally separate from md-optimizer because xTB is not a periodic MD workflow.

agents.title: VASP Executor
agents.role: Prepare or submit DFT jobs through the normalized VASP skill.
agents.use_when: Use when electronic-structure fidelity is required.
notes: The normalized VASP skill already supports direct setup, submit, run, and parse entrypoints.

agents.title: Structure Generator
agents.role: Generate candidate frameworks through PORMAKE-based workflows.
agents.use_when: Use when the project needs new MOF, COF, or HOF candidates.

agents.title: Analyst
agents.role: Interpret completed results, correlate physics across workflows, and surface gaps.
agents.use_when: Use when calculations have produced artifacts and the user wants interpretation.
workflow: If the question asks for mechanism, benchmarks, or parameter rationale, query `literature-rag` before concluding.
notes: Use the local literature RAG before drawing mechanism or benchmark conclusions that go beyond the raw result files.

agents.title: Supervisor
agents.role: Observe cluster jobs and run directories without mutating project state.
agents.use_when: Use for job-status checks and failure-signature collection.
